messages.text: Rinderknech denies refusing doping test and expects to be cleared

metadata.summary: France's Arthur Rinderknech is confident he will be cleared of an alleged refusal to undergo a doping test.
metadata.content: Arthur Rinderknech denies refusing to take anti-doping test after charge confirmed for French tennis player | Tennis News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Arthur Rinderknech denies refusing to take anti-doping test after charge confirmed for French tennis player French newspaper L'Equipe reported Arthur Rinderknech's alleged refusal to take doping test; International ‌Tennis Integrity Agency has since confirmed charge; former ⁠Wimbledon champion Marketa Vondrousova handed four-year ban in June after tribunal found she refused test Wednesday 25 November 2026 11:15, UK Image: France's Arthur Rinderknech has denied refusing to take an anti-doping test in June France's Arthur Rinderknech is confident he will be cleared of an alleged refusal to undergo a doping test. The International ‌Tennis Integrity Agency [ITIA] confirmed on Wednesday that the 31-year-old had been charged for refusing a test in Brittany in June after French newspaper L'Equipe initially reported in their story that he was facing a four-year ban. Rinderknech denied the allegation on Instagram, while stressing that he has never taken a banned substance and revealing he has asked for the ​matter to be heard by an independent tribunal. Yoro's one-match suspension for the red card he was shown in the 4-0 defeat at Anfield has been removed, despite referees' chief Howard Webb supporting the decision to send him off. Man Utd will contact ProRef and the Premier League directly over what they believe to be a 'totally wrong' interpretation of Yoro's red card against Liverpool. messages.text: Sky announces Game Changing coalition for women and girls in sport

metadata.summary: Sky is pleased to announce the formation of the Game Changing coalition, a new UK initiative to drive lasting change for women and girls through increased participation in sport.
metadata.content: Sky announces Game Changing coalition to drive lasting change in UK for women and girls through sport | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Sky announces Game Changing coalition to drive lasting change in UK for women and girls through sport Sky has announced the Game Changing coalition for women and girls in sport; the group, convened by Sky, aims to improve participation of girls in comparison to their male counterparts; girls still spend 1.4 fewer hours playing sport than boys per week Tuesday 24 November 2026 11:53, UK Image: The Game Changing coalition is a new UK initiative to drive lasting change for women and girls through increased participation in sport Sky is pleased to announce the formation of the Game Changing coalition, a new UK initiative to drive lasting change for women and girls through increased participation in sport. Despite growing visibility and investment in women's sport, Sky's Game Changing report shows that girls still spend 1.4 fewer hours per week playing sport than boys - equivalent to every girl being sidelined for 52 football matches per year compared to their male counterparts. While landmark sporting moments have captured the nation's imagination, this surge in interest has not translated into enough girls regularly engaging in sport. metadata.summary: Charley Hull tasted defeat on WTGL debut as her Atlanta Drive side lost 8-3 to Lottie Woad's Boston Common at the SoFi Center in Florida.
metadata.content: WTGL: Charley Hull 'has great laugh' on Atlanta Drive debut despite defeat to Lottie Woad's Boston Common | Golf News | Sky Sports Skip to main content WTGL: Charley Hull 'has great laugh' on Atlanta Drive debut despite defeat to Lottie Woad's Boston Common Charley Hull off to Disney World after making first appearance at the SoFi Center; Englishwoman wins her opening singles match, against Solheim Cup team-mate Celine Boutier, but Atlanta Drive soundly beaten by Boston Common; watch every WTGL match live on Sky Sports Wednesday 25 November 2026 06:41, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Charley Hull started her WTGL debut in some style with this brilliant tee shot Charley Hull tasted defeat on WTGL debut as her Atlanta Drive side lost 8-3 to Lottie Woad's Boston Common at the SoFi Center in Florida. English star Hull won her first singles match in the competition, beating Solheim Cup team-mate Celine Boutier as she holed a 15-foot return putt having shot an initial effort way past the hole. But Atlanta Drive were still soundly defeated in their first game of the inaugural women's season as Boston Common bounced back from last week's loss to Motor City.
